correctness.rationale: Adjacent window differences give D_k|E_k with second endpoint constant 27. For even k the Lucas state (x,y)=(L_{k+1},L_{k+2}) lies on y²-xy-x²=5: this quadratic form reverses sign under the recurrence. If p≡2 mod 3, cubing is injective; for p≡1 mod 3 write (x,y)=(ω^i,3ω^j). Independently reducing the conic defect in the basis (1,ω), the four conjugacy representatives (i,j)=(0,1),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2) give coefficient pairs (-15,-12),(5,-2),(-10,-5),(-7,10), with norms 189,39,75,219. Their only relevant prime divisors in the split case are 7,13,73 (p=5 belongs to the injective case). Thus outside the stated bad set the endpoint roots are 1 and 3, and the other factors of the cube differences are units mod p, yielding the same endpoint congruences mod p^e. The linear recurrence yields a return to (2,1) mod p^e. Direct substitution gives H(u,v)-H(v,u+v)=2v³, so every window sum is zero mod p^e. The monic polynomial formed from the Binet cubic roots is (T²-4T-1)(T²+T-1), justifying the exact four-window gcd. Fresh integer recurrence and gcd of the four literal windows give (D,E)=(2,28),(1080,28080),(3571,260683) at k=6,24,34. Independent modular recurrence gives state return (2,1), zero endpoint differences, and base window residues 3,4,11 respectively modulo 7,13,73; period sums vanish by telescoping. This verifies the infinite witness progressions, without asserting optimality at 2 or 3.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by a prior attempt to replace an infinite family of consecutive cube sums by two endpoint differences. The theorem measures exactly where that shortcut is reliable prime-adically, uniformly in even length, and proves that three surprising exceptional primes cannot be eliminated by ignoring small initial lengths. This remains useful information about the endpoint surrogate even given an exact formula for the window gcd itself.
